candidate.title: Digital RNA / HiRes-Seq / FREQ-Seq / RNAtag-Seq
candidate.scope: The assigned middle row of the Illumina poster, a grouped explanatory schematic of barcode-bearing cDNA, preferential amplification, sequencing, and barcode-based recovery of relative RNA abundance. All four printed target names are retained as distinct assays, not aliases. The graph preserves the drawn route and its two separately processed cDNA exemplars; its molecule-counting interpretation is supported for Digital RNA at this schematic scope. The matched primary sources resolve specific misapplications of this route to HiRes-Seq, FREQ-Seq, and RNAtag-Seq in method_scopes and corrections. For those three targets, separate primary-supported sequencing/readout interfaces retain their actual input-library history and barcode meaning; these are explicit corrective interpretations, not additional branches claimed to be drawn. Their unshown complete workflows are not added. The adjacent UMI Method row above, MARS-Seq row below, clipped text above, and chemistry panel at the right are neighboring material, not target alternatives or connected branches. RNA-to-cDNA preparation is an input history, not a drawn operation.

states.label: RNAtag-Seq cDNA library retaining RNA-sample barcodes
features: Primary-supported input history, not a new depicted preparation branch: fragmented RNA receives sample-identifying adapters by ligation, tagged RNAs are pooled and rRNA depleted, and adapter-primed reverse transcription converts RNA to cDNA.
RNA degradation and second-adapter ligation to single-stranded cDNA precede PCR that supplies full Illumina sequencing-adapter sequences.

Initial RNA adapters have a 5′ phosphate and a 3′ blocking group; this end chemistry belongs to the primary-supported RNA interface, not the poster’s post-cDNA adapter icons.

evidence.locator: [b00006], main text: RNAtag-Seq introduction
